Good, let's dig into this — but first, a mechanical fact that constrains all three of your options: because of what's already cut, **there's already a continuous open channel** at every LOWER tab, from the plate's bottom face (Z=0) straight up through the M3 hole (Z=0→2.5) into the open hex pocket cavity (Z=2.5→5). Nothing stops a peg pushed up from underneath until it reaches the top of the pocket at Z=5. So whatever we design has to work *with* that channel, not against it.

## Cross-section: keep hex
No downside worth chasing here. It's already cut into 16 tabs, it gives you anti-rotation for free (useful if you're turning a screw one-handed), and switching to round buys you nothing while costing a re-cut. Keep hex.

## The two retention ideas — and the problem they share

**Option A (rounded bump near the tip)** and **Option B (necked-down through-peg)** are actually the same mechanism at heart: something wider than the hole has to end up *on the far side* of the hole. For FDM that means one of two things:

1. **Print it oversized and force it through** — a snap-fit. This depends on interference tolerance you haven't measured yet (you've printed zero coupons so far), PETG's flex-fatigue behavior under repeated insertion (module swap is one of your own pass criteria, T16, <60s — a snap you can't re-open easily fails that test), and it risks cracking the pillar or chipping the plate edge if it's too tight, or falling out if it's too loose. You get exactly one shot at reading the fit correctly, with no time buffer to iterate a whole new pillar print.
2. **Two-piece assembly / heat-staking** — print the peg straight through, then deform or add the retention head after. That's an extra manufacturing step and extra tooling you haven't budgeted for in the Sétif window.

This is the *exact* failure mode your own spec already ruled out for Smart Blocks: *"No peg-into-hole gripping — FDM hole tolerance is too loose and inconsistent to grip on reliably."* Same physics, same printer, same risk — except a pillar carries structural load for the whole chassis, so a bad fit here is worse than a bad fit on a sensor block.

## What I'd propose instead (PROPOSED, not cut yet)

Use the channel that's already there for an **M3 screw**, not a snap peg:
- Hex tenon on the pillar plugs into the hex pocket (anti-rotation, already-cut geometry, zero rework)
- A bore through the pillar's center lines up with the M3 hole
- Screw goes in from the bottom face of the plate, up through the floor hole, through the pillar's bore, into a nut or heat-set insert
- Retention is positive and adjustable, not dependent on guessing a friction fit correctly on the first print
- You're already buying M3 hardware for everything else, so this adds no new shopping list item
- Disassembly is a screwdriver, well under your 60-second module-swap target, and it's the same "boring, available, already-working" call you made for motors and drivers

Before I model it, two things only you can answer:

content.text:
Good — "no tools" + "removable both ends" actually rules out both the plain hand-screwdriver M3 approach *and* the snap/neck-down ideas (snap fights the "removable" requirement; a bare screw fights "no tools"). There's a standard solution that satisfies both without touching untested print tolerances:

## Proposed mechanism: heat-set insert + thumbscrew

- **Pillar:** hex tenon each end (as already planned), each tenon has a coaxial bore
- **Insert:** an M3 brass heat-set threaded insert pressed into each tenon end *after* printing (melted in with a soldering iron — which is already on your shopping list)
- **Fastener:** an M3 **knurled thumbscrew** (hand-tightened, no driver) through the plate's existing floor hole, threading into that insert

Why this beats the snap/neck-down ideas for your situation:
- **Retention comes from threads, not friction/interference** — so it doesn't depend on a print tolerance you haven't measured yet. Thread engagement is forgiving of the same 0.1–0.3mm FDM variance that would break a snap fit.
- **Genuinely tool-free** (thumbscrew, hand-tightened) and **independently removable at both ends** — pulls a plate off in seconds, satisfies your T16 module-swap test.
- **Reuses the channel and hex pocket you already cut** — zero rework on the plate.
- **New hardware is cheap and small**: 16× M3 heat-set inserts + M3 thumbscrews. Worth adding to the Sétif list — I'd treat this as a shopping list addition, not a redesign.

Fallback if heat-set inserts turn out to be hard to find locally: a **quarter-turn bayonet** (twist-lock, like a GoPro mount) is the other tool-free option that doesn't rely on friction tolerance — geometric interference instead of a press-fit — but it's more complex to model and less forgiving to get right on one print attempt. I'd only go there if inserts are a dead end.

One number I still need from you, since it's OPEN in your spec and directly sizes the pillar's shaft:

content.text:
22mm it is — right in your range, and I'll flag it clearly so you can nudge it later (single parameter, trivial to change).

Now modeling the pillar. Two things I'm choosing without a firm number yet, both flagged as **NEEDS VERIFICATION**:

- **Tenon size:** 5.7mm across flats (0.3mm undersize vs. the 6.0mm nominal pocket) — printed holes come out undersized and printed external pegs tend to come out at-or-over nominal, so a tenon cut at the same 6.0mm as the socket almost certainly won't fit. This undersize is a placeholder until your test coupon gives real numbers.
- **Insert bore:** Ø4.2mm × 5mm deep, a common size for M3 heat-set inserts — but exact inserts vary by brand. Send me the datasheet/listing once you've picked one and I'll correct this to match exactly; too loose and it spins, too tight and it splits the tenon on insertion.

Shoulder is a 10mm-across-flats hex (bears flat on the tab face, stops the tenon 0.3mm short of the pocket floor so it seats on the shoulder, not by bottoming out). Overall length: 2.2 (tenon) + 22 (shaft/spacing) + 2.2 (tenon) = 26.4mm.

import adsk.core, adsk.fusion, math, json, traceback

def run(context):
    try:
        app = adsk.core.Application.get()
        design = app.activeProduct
        root = design.rootComponent
        log = {}

        # clean up prior attempt if present
        for occ in list(root.occurrences):
            if occ.component.name == 'HexPillar':
                occ.deleteMe()

        occs = root.occurrences
        trans = adsk.core.Matrix3D.create()
        newOcc = occs.addNewComponent(trans)
        comp = newOcc.component
        comp.name = 'HexPillar'

        TENON_AF = 5.7      # across-flats, mm -- NEEDS TESTING vs coupon
        SHAFT_AF = 10.0     # across-flats, mm
        TENON_H  = 2.2       # mm, into pocket (pocket is 2.5mm deep -> 0.3mm clearance)
        SPACING  = 22.0      # mm, plate-to-plate gap (user-selected, within 20-25 range)
        BORE_D   = 4.2       # mm -- PLACEHOLDER, verify vs actual insert datasheet
        BORE_DEPTH = 5.0     # mm

        def hex_pts(af, z_cm):
            R = (af/2.0) / math.cos(math.radians(30))
            pts = []
            for k in range(6):
                ang = math.radians(30 + 60*k)
                pts.append(adsk.core.Point3D.create((R*math.cos(ang))/10.0, (R*math.sin(ang))/10.0, z_cm))
            return pts

        def hex_extrude(af, z0_mm, h_mm, name):
            pl_in = comp.constructionPlanes.createInput()
            pl_in.setByOffset(comp.xYConstructionPlane, adsk.core.ValueInput.createByReal(z0_mm/10.0))
            pl = comp.constructionPlanes.add(pl_in)
            sk = comp.sketches.add(pl)
            sk.name = 'SK_'+name
            pts = hex_pts(af, 0)
            lines = sk.sketchCurves.sketchLines
            first = lines.addByTwoPoints(pts[0], pts[1])
            prev = first.endSketchPoint
            for k in range(1,5):
                prev = lines.addByTwoPoints(prev, pts[k+1]).endSketchPoint
            lines.addByTwoPoints(prev, first.startSketchPoint)
            prof = sk.profiles.item(0)
            exts = comp.features.extrudeFeatures
            ei = exts.createInput(prof, adsk.fusion.FeatureOperations.NewBodyFeatureOperation if name=='Tenon1' else adsk.fusion.FeatureOperations.JoinFeatureOperation)
            ei.setDistanceExtent(False, adsk.core.ValueInput.createByReal(h_mm/10.0))
            f = exts.add(ei)
            f.name = name
            return f

        hex_extrude(TENON_AF, 0.0, TENON_H, 'Tenon1')
        hex_extrude(SHAFT_AF, TENON_H, SPACING, 'Shaft')
        hex_extrude(TENON_AF, TENON_H+SPACING, TENON_H, 'Tenon2')

        body = comp.bRepBodies.item(0)
        body.name = 'HexPillar_Body'

        total_h = TENON_H*2 + SPACING

        # bore from bottom
        sk1 = comp.sketches.add(comp.xYConstructionPlane)
        sk1.name = 'SK_Bore1'
        sk1.sketchCurves.sketchCircles.addByCenterRadius(adsk.core.Point3D.create(0,0,0), (BORE_D/2.0)/10.0)
        prof1 = sk1.profiles.item(0)
        exts = comp.features.extrudeFeatures
        ei1 = exts.createInput(prof1, adsk.fusion.FeatureOperations.CutFeatureOperation)
        ei1.participantBodies = [body]
        ei1.setDistanceExtent(False, adsk.core.ValueInput.createByReal(BORE_DEPTH/10.0))
        exts.add(ei1).name = 'Bore_Bottom'

        # bore from top
        pl_in = comp.constructionPlanes.createInput()
        pl_in.setByOffset(comp.xYConstructionPlane, adsk.core.ValueInput.createByReal(total_h/10.0))
        pl_top = comp.constructionPlanes.add(pl_in)
        sk2 = comp.sketches.add(pl_top)
        sk2.name = 'SK_Bore2'
        sk2.sketchCurves.sketchCircles.addByCenterRadius(adsk.core.Point3D.create(0,0,0), (BORE_D/2.0)/10.0)
        prof2 = sk2.profiles.item(0)
        ei2 = exts.createInput(prof2, adsk.fusion.FeatureOperations.CutFeatureOperation)
        ei2.participantBodies = [body]
        ei2.setDistanceExtent(False, adsk.core.ValueInput.createByReal(-BORE_DEPTH/10.0))
        exts.add(ei2).name = 'Bore_Top'

        log['total_length_mm'] = total_h
        log['volume_cm3'] = round(body.physicalProperties.volume, 4)
        log['bbox_mm'] = [round((body.boundingBox.maxPoint.x-body.boundingBox.minPoint.x)*10,3),
                          round((body.boundingBox.maxPoint.y-body.boundingBox.minPoint.y)*10,3),
                          round((body.boundingBox.maxPoint.z-body.boundingBox.minPoint.z)*10,3)]
        print(json.dumps(log))
    except:
        print('ERROR: ' + traceback.format_exc())

import adsk.core, adsk.fusion, math, json, traceback

def run(context):
    try:
        app = adsk.core.Application.get()
        design = app.activeProduct
        root = design.rootComponent
        log = {}

        # clean up any partial bodies/sketches/planes from the failed attempt
        for name in ['Tenon1','Shaft','Tenon2','Bore_Bottom','Bore_Top']:
            for f in list(root.features.extrudeFeatures):
                if f.name == name:
                    f.deleteMe()
        for name in ['SK_Tenon1','SK_Shaft','SK_Tenon2','SK_Bore1','SK_Bore2']:
            s = root.sketches.itemByName(name)
            if s: s.deleteMe()
        for name in ['PL_Tenon1','PL_Shaft','PL_Tenon2','PL_Bore2']:
            for p in list(root.constructionPlanes):
                if p.name == name:
                    p.deleteMe()
        for b in list(root.bRepBodies):
            if b.name.startswith('HexPillar'):
                b.deleteMe()

        TENON_AF = 5.7
        SHAFT_AF = 10.0
        TENON_H  = 2.2
        SPACING  = 22.0
        BORE_D   = 4.2
        BORE_DEPTH = 5.0

        # place the pillar far from the plate (plate spans roughly -105..105 in X/Y) so it's visually separate
        OX, OY = 200.0, 0.0

        def hex_pts(af, ox, oy):
            R = (af/2.0) / math.cos(math.radians(30))
            pts = []
            for k in range(6):
                ang = math.radians(30 + 60*k)
                pts.append(adsk.core.Point3D.create((ox + R*math.cos(ang))/10.0, (oy + R*math.sin(ang))/10.0, 0))
            return pts

        def hex_extrude(af, z0_mm, h_mm, name, op):
            pl_in = root.constructionPlanes.createInput()
            pl_in.setByOffset(root.xYConstructionPlane, adsk.core.ValueInput.createByReal(z0_mm/10.0))
            pl = root.constructionPlanes.add(pl_in)
            pl.name = 'PL_'+name
            sk = root.sketches.add(pl)
            sk.name = 'SK_'+name
            pts = hex_pts(af, OX, OY)
            lines = sk.sketchCurves.sketchLines
            first = lines.addByTwoPoints(pts[0], pts[1])
            prev = first.endSketchPoint
            for k in range(1,5):
                prev = lines.addByTwoPoints(prev, pts[k+1]).endSketchPoint
            lines.addByTwoPoints(prev, first.startSketchPoint)
            prof = sk.profiles.item(0)
            exts = root.features.extrudeFeatures
            ei = exts.createInput(prof, op)
            if op == adsk.fusion.FeatureOperations.JoinFeatureOperation:
                bodies = [b for b in root.bRepBodies if b.name == 'HexPillar_Body']
                ei.participantBodies = bodies
            ei.setDistanceExtent(False, adsk.core.ValueInput.createByReal(h_mm/10.0))
            f = exts.add(ei)
            f.name = name
            return f

        hex_extrude(TENON_AF, 0.0, TENON_H, 'Tenon1', adsk.fusion.FeatureOperations.NewBodyFeatureOperation)
        newbody = None
        for b in root.bRepBodies:
            if b.name.startswith('Body') and b not in []:
                pass
        # rename the newest body (last one added)
        body = root.bRepBodies.item(root.bRepBodies.count - 1)
        body.name = 'HexPillar_Body'

content.text:
Yes — you should be worried, and the physics backs that up clearly. Let me walk through why, because the length change matters a lot more than it might seem.

## Why a taller pillar is a real risk (not just aesthetics)

When something hits the top plate sideways, the pillar acts as a cantilever beam fixed at the bottom tenon. The stress at that root joint scales with **force × length** — so doubling the pillar length doubles the stress from the same bump, for the same force.

There's a second factor that makes this worse for a *printed* part specifically: a pillar printed standing upright has its layer lines horizontal. A sideways hit pulls those layers apart in tension — which is the weakest direction for FDM parts (layer adhesion is typically the first thing to fail, well before the bulk material would). So a tall vertical pillar hit sideways is stressed exactly on its weakest axis.

Running the numbers for your 10mm-across-flats hex shaft, order-of-magnitude:

| Pillar length | Approx. lateral force to reach ~20 MPa at the root (conservative FDM interlayer limit) |
|---|---|
| **22 mm** | ~95 N (≈ 9.7 kgf) — a hard deliberate shove |
| **200 mm** | ~10 N (≈ 1.1 kgf) — a light nudge |

That's roughly a **9× drop** in the force needed to stress the joint, just from the length change. At 200mm, an accidental bump against furniture or the robot tipping against something could snap a pillar at the root. (8 pillars share the load in reality, so real capacity is higher than a single-pillar worst case — but the ratio between 22mm and 200mm doesn't change.)

## There's a second, separate problem at 200mm

Your plate is **210mm wide**. A 200mm gap between plates makes the chassis almost as tall as it is wide — on top of whatever height the wheels/motors/lower-plate hardware already add. That's a tall, top-heavy structure for a small TT-gearmotor robot moving at "human walking pace." Independent of pillar bending, **the whole robot becomes much easier to tip over** just by turning or nudging an obstacle — a real risk for a live defense demo.

## My read on the mm/cm mix-up

I think you're right that this was a unit slip, but I'd push back on "20cm" as the fix too — your own spec already had a number for this: **"Plate spacing, M3 standoffs, 30–50mm (PROPOSED)."** 200mm isn't a typo-correction back to that, it's 4–6× beyond it.

content.text:
I pulled everything publicly available. Note upfront: **ROBOTIS doesn't publish plate-level dimensions** (outer size, thickness, grid pitch, hole diameters) in any accessible source — those live in their Onshape CAD and a technical-drawing PDF behind robotis.com. So the plate-geometry rows below are marked unconfirmed. Everything else is solid.

## A. Directly comparable — and actionable

| Dimension | Ours (measured) | TurtleBot3 | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Plate spacing / standoff** | **100 mm** | **35 mm and 45 mm** (`SUPPORT_HEX_M3_0XL35_FF`, `_0XL45_FF`) | ⚠️ **Adapt to ~40 mm** |
| **Total robot height** | ~150–160 mm projected (10+100+10 deck stack + motors/wheels) | **141 mm** total *including wheels and LiDAR* | ⚠️ We'd be taller than TB3 with a far less capable robot |
| **Fastener standard** | M3 (Ø3.2 clearance) | M3×8 bolts + M3 nuts | ✅ Already aligned |
| **Standoff cross-section** | 10 mm AF hex shaft | M3 hex standoff (~5.5–6 mm AF) | ✅ Keep ours — justified deviation |
| **Max traversable step** | n/a | 10 mm | reference point for your wheel sizing |

**On spacing — the numbers if you adopt 40 mm:**

| | 100 mm (current) | 40 mm (TB3-aligned) |
|---|---|---|
| Lateral force to reach stress limit | ~21 N (2.1 kgf) | **~52 N (5.3 kgf)** — 2.5× stronger |
| Pillar volume each | 8.65 cm³ | **3.45 cm³** |
| Material for 8 pillars | 69.2 cm³ | **27.6 cm³** (~42 cm³ saved) |
| Deck stack height | 120 mm | **60 mm** |

Keeping the 10 mm AF shaft (vs TB3's ~5.5 mm) is worth defending in your report: you're FDM-printing in PETG where TB3 injection-molds, so you need more cross-section for equivalent stiffness. That's a deliberate, explainable deviation.

## B. Architectural differences — can't adapt (plate is frozen)

| Aspect | Ours | TurtleBot3 | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Plate architecture** | 1 monolithic 210×210 mm plate | **24 small plates tiled together** | Your half-lap hex tabs were designed for tiling — but you have nothing to tile with. They're now repurposed as standoff mounts. **Expect a jury question here.** |
| **Hole system** | Irregular/decorative, no pitch | Regular grid (the entire point of a "waffle") | Biggest functional divergence; will matter most when you design Smart Blocks |
| **Plate thickness** | 10 mm | Thin, injection-molded (unconfirmed) | Drives print time and weight — see below |
| **Material** | PETG, FDM | Injection-molded engineering plastic | Ours needs more material for equivalent stiffness |

## C. Print-time reality check — the finding I'd act on second

Community reports for 3D-printing a **TB3 waffle plate: 7–10 hours each** — and that's one of their *small* plates. Yours is roughly **10× the volume** (232.36 cm³ measured).

Rough estimate for your plate: **~13–20 hours each, so 26–40 hours for two.** Your own spec doc set the plate size budget at *"~4h print time"* — the current design is far past that, on a printer you share with your friend, inside a two-week hardware window.

Also: TB3's design explicitly *"doesn't need additional support material."* Yours does — the 8 UPPER hex tabs are unsupported 15 mm cantilevers. That's a regression against the reference design, and it's baked into the frozen plate.

## D. What I'd actually change

| Priority | Change | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | Pillar spacing **100 mm → 40 mm** | Matches proven TB3 geometry, 2.5× stronger, 42 cm³ less material, keeps you under TB3's total height |

        design = app.activeProduct

        log = {'active_doc': doc.name}

        for name in ['PillarBore_Top','PillarBore_Bottom','PillarTenon2','PillarShaft','PillarTenon1']:
            for f in list(root.features.extrudeFeatures):
                if f.name == name:

        for name in ['SK_PillarBore2','SK_PillarBore1','SK_PillarTenon2','SK_PillarShaft','SK_PillarTenon1']:
            s = root.sketches.itemByName(name)
            if s: s.deleteMe()
        for name in ['PL_PillarBore2','PL_PillarTenon2','PL_PillarShaft','PL_PillarTenon1']:
            for p in list(root.constructionPlanes):
                if p.name == name:
                    p.deleteMe()
        for b in list(root.bRepBodies):
            if b.name.startswith('HexPillar'):
                b.deleteMe()

        TENON_AF = 5.7
        SHAFT_AF = 10.0
        TENON_H  = 2.2
        SPACING  = 40.0
        BORE_D   = 4.2
        BORE_DEPTH = 5.0
        OX, OY = 0.0, 0.0

        def hex_pts(af, ox, oy):
            R = (af/2.0) / math.cos(math.radians(30))
            return [adsk.core.Point3D.create((ox + R*math.cos(math.radians(30+60*k)))/10.0,
                                             (oy + R*math.sin(math.radians(30+60*k)))/10.0, 0) for k in range(6)]

        def hex_extrude(af, z0_mm, h_mm, name, op):
            pin = root.constructionPlanes.createInput()
            pin.setByOffset(root.xYConstructionPlane, adsk.core.ValueInput.createByReal(z0_mm/10.0))
            pl = root.constructionPlanes.add(pin); pl.name = 'PL_'+name
            sk = root.sketches.add(pl); sk.name = 'SK_'+name
            pts = hex_pts(af, OX, OY)
            lines = sk.sketchCurves.sketchLines
            first = lines.addByTwoPoints(pts[0], pts[1])
            prev = first.endSketchPoint
            for k in range(1,5):
                prev = lines.addByTwoPoints(prev, pts[k+1]).endSketchPoint
            lines.addByTwoPoints(prev, first.startSketchPoint)
            exts = root.features.extrudeFeatures
            ei = exts.createInput(sk.profiles.item(0), op)
            if op == adsk.fusion.FeatureOperations.JoinFeatureOperation:

            ei.setDistanceExtent(False, adsk.core.ValueInput.createByReal(h_mm/10.0))

        body.name = 'HexPillar_Body'
        hex_extrude(SHAFT_AF, TENON_H, SPACING, 'PillarShaft', adsk.fusion.FeatureOperations.JoinFeatureOperation)
        hex_extrude(TENON_AF, TENON_H+SPACING, TENON_H, 'PillarTenon2', adsk.fusion.FeatureOperations.JoinFeatureOperation)

        total_h = TENON_H*2 + SPACING
        exts = root.features.extrudeFeatures

        sk1 = root.sketches.add(root.xYConstructionPlane); sk1.name = 'SK_PillarBore1'
        sk1.sketchCurves.sketchCircles.addByCenterRadius(adsk.core.Point3D.create(OX/10.0, OY/10.0, 0), (BORE_D/2.0)/10.0)
        ei1 = exts.createInput(sk1.profiles.item(0), adsk.fusion.FeatureOperations.CutFeatureOperation)
        ei1.participantBodies = [body]
        ei1.setDistanceExtent(False, adsk.core.ValueInput.createByReal(BORE_DEPTH/10.0))
        exts.add(ei1).name = 'PillarBore_Bottom'

        pin = root.constructionPlanes.createInput()
        pin.setByOffset(root.xYConstructionPlane, adsk.core.ValueInput.createByReal(total_h/10.0))
        pl_top = root.constructionPlanes.add(pin); pl_top.name = 'PL_PillarBore2'
        sk2 = root.sketches.add(pl_top); sk2.name = 'SK_PillarBore2'
        sk2.sketchCurves.sketchCircles.addByCenterRadius(adsk.core.Point3D.create(OX/10.0, OY/10.0, 0), (BORE_D/2.0)/10.0)
        ei2 = exts.createInput(sk2.profiles.item(0), adsk.fusion.FeatureOperations.CutFeatureOperation)
        ei2.participantBodies = [body]
        ei2.setDistanceExtent(False, adsk.core.ValueInput.createByReal(-BORE_DEPTH/10.0))
        exts.add(ei2).name = 'PillarBore_Top'

        bb = body.boundingBox
        log['shaft_length_mm'] = SPACING
        log['total_length_mm'] = total_h
        log['volume_cm3'] = round(body.physicalProperties.volume, 4)
        log['bbox_mm'] = [round((bb.maxPoint.x-bb.minPoint.x)*10,3), round((bb.maxPoint.y-bb.minPoint.y)*10,3), round((bb.maxPoint.z-bb.minPoint.z)*10,3)]
        print(json.dumps(log))
    except:
        print('ERROR: ' + traceback.format_exc())

def run(context):
    try:
        app = adsk.core.Application.get()
        doc = app.activeDocument
        assert doc.name == 'waffle plate', 'WRONG DOC: ' + doc.name
        root = app.activeProduct.rootComponent
        body = [b for b in root.bRepBodies if b.name=='Body1'][0]
        log = {'doc': doc.name}

        # cleanup prior run
        for nm in ['TopMark_T','BottomMark_B']:
            for f in list(root.features.extrudeFeatures):
                if f.name == nm: f.deleteMe()
        for nm in ['SK_TopMark_T','SK_BottomMark_B']:
            s = root.sketches.itemByName(nm)
            if s: s.deleteMe()
        for nm in ['PL_TopMark','PL_BottomMark']:
            for p in list(root.constructionPlanes):
                if p.name == nm: p.deleteMe()

        FONT = 'Bahnschrift'
        H = 1.8          # cm = 18mm
        DEPTH = 0.08     # cm = 0.8mm
        CX, CY = 0.0, 1.5   # cm -> world (0,15)mm
        HW, HH = 1.1, 1.2   # half box cm

        exts = root.features.extrudeFeatures

        def add_text(plane, name, letter, cut_dist):
            sk = root.sketches.add(plane)
            sk.name = 'SK_' + name
            ti = sk.sketchTexts.createInput2(letter, H)
            corner = adsk.core.Point3D.create(CX-HW, CY-HH, 0)
            diag   = adsk.core.Point3D.create(CX+HW, CY+HH, 0)
            ti.setAsMultiLine(corner, diag,
                              adsk.core.HorizontalAlignments.CenterHorizontalAlignment,
                              adsk.core.VerticalAlignments.MiddleVerticalAlignment, 0)
            ti.fontName = FONT
            st = sk.sketchTexts.add(ti)
            ei = exts.createInput(st, adsk.fusion.FeatureOperations.CutFeatureOperation)
            ei.participantBodies = [body]
            ei.setDistanceExtent(False, adsk.core.ValueInput.createByReal(cut_dist))
            f = exts.add(ei)
            f.name = name
            return sk.profiles.count

        # TOP: plane at Z=10mm, normal +Z, cut downward
        pin = root.constructionPlanes.createInput()
        pin.setByOffset(root.xYConstructionPlane, adsk.core.ValueInput.createByReal(1.0))
        pl_top = root.constructionPlanes.add(pin); pl_top.name = 'PL_TopMark'
        log['top_profiles'] = add_text(pl_top, 'TopMark_T', 'T', -DEPTH)

        # BOTTOM: plane at Z=0, normal -Z, u=-X v=+Y so text reads correctly from below
        pgeom = adsk.core.Plane.create(adsk.core.Point3D.create(0,0,0),
                                       adsk.core.Vector3D.create(0,0,-1))
        okuv = pgeom.setUVDirections(adsk.core.Vector3D.create(-1,0,0),
                                     adsk.core.Vector3D.create(0,1,0))
        log['setUV_ok'] = okuv
        pin2 = root.constructionPlanes.createInput()
        pin2.setByPlane(pgeom)
        pl_bot = root.constructionPlanes.add(pin2); pl_bot.name = 'PL_BottomMark'
        log['bottom_profiles'] = add_text(pl_bot, 'BottomMark_B', 'B', -DEPTH)

        log['volume_cm3'] = round(body.physicalProperties.volume, 4)
        print(json.dumps(log))
    except:
        print('ERROR: ' + traceback.format_exc())

        assert doc.name == 'waffle plate', 'WRONG DOC: ' + doc.name
        root = app.activeProduct.rootComponent
        body = [b for b in root.bRepBodies if b.name=='Body1'][0]
        log = {'doc': doc.name}

        # cleanup prior run
        for nm in ['TopMark_T','BottomMark_B']:
            for f in list(root.features.extrudeFeatures):
                if f.name == nm: f.deleteMe()
        for nm in ['SK_TopMark_T','SK_BottomMark_B']:
            s = root.sketches.itemByName(nm)
            if s: s.deleteMe()
        for nm in ['PL_TopMark','PL_BottomMark']:
            for p in list(root.constructionPlanes):
                if p.name == nm: p.deleteMe()

        FONT = 'Bahnschrift'
        H = 1.8          # cm = 18mm
        DEPTH = 0.08     # cm = 0.8mm
        CX, CY = 0.0, 1.5   # cm -> world (0,15)mm
        HW, HH = 1.1, 1.2   # half box cm

        exts = root.features.extrudeFeatures

        def add_text(plane, name, letter, cut_dist):
            sk = root.sketches.add(plane)
            sk.name = 'SK_' + name
            ti = sk.sketchTexts.createInput2(letter, H)
            corner = adsk.core.Point3D.create(CX-HW, CY-HH, 0)
            diag   = adsk.core.Point3D.create(CX+HW, CY+HH, 0)
            ti.setAsMultiLine(corner, diag,
                              adsk.core.HorizontalAlignments.CenterHorizontalAlignment,
                              adsk.core.VerticalAlignments.MiddleVerticalAlignment, 0)
            ti.fontName = FONT
            st = sk.sketchTexts.add(ti)
            ei = exts.createInput(st, adsk.fusion.FeatureOperations.CutFeatureOperation)
            ei.participantBodies = [body]
            ei.setDistanceExtent(False, adsk.core.ValueInput.createByReal(cut_dist))
            f = exts.add(ei)
            f.name = name
            return sk.profiles.count

        # TOP: plane at Z=10mm, normal +Z, cut downward
        pin = root.constructionPlanes.createInput()
        pin.setByOffset(root.xYConstructionPlane, adsk.core.ValueInput.createByReal(1.0))
        pl_top = root.constructionPlanes.add(pin); pl_top.name = 'PL_TopMark'
        log['top_profiles'] = add_text(pl_top, 'TopMark_T', 'T', -DEPTH)

        # BOTTOM: plane at Z=0, normal -Z, u=-X v=+Y so text reads correctly from below
        pgeom = adsk.core.Plane.create(adsk.core.Point3D.create(0,0,0),
                                       adsk.core.Vector3D.create(0,0,-1))
        okuv = pgeom.setUVDirections(adsk.core.Vector3D.create(-1,0,0),
                                     adsk.core.Vector3D.create(0,1,0))
        log['setUV_ok'] = okuv
        pin2 = root.constructionPlanes.createInput()
        pin2.setByPlane(pgeom)
        pl_bot = root.constructionPlanes.add(pin2); pl_bot.name = 'PL_BottomMark'
        log['bottom_profiles'] = add_text(pl_bot, 'BottomMark_B', 'B', -DEPTH)

        log['volume_cm3'] = round(body.physicalProperties.volume, 4)
        print(json.dumps(log))
    except:
        print('ERROR: ' + traceback.format_exc())

Good instinct on the weak point — let's separate the three ideas, because one of them is solid, one has real risk given what you've already committed to, and one might already be exactly what we planned.

## 1. "Make the plate-side part thick so it's not a weak point" — you're right, and here's the actual fix

The current design (5.7mm tenon stepping up to a 10mm shaft) does have a real stress concentration — right at that sudden step, at Z=2.2mm. But thickening the tenon itself is capped: it has to fit inside the **hex pocket already cut into your real plate**, which is fixed at 6.0mm across flats. We can't make the tenon much bigger without re-cutting the plate, which you've ruled out.

The actual fix for a stress concentration at a step isn't more material at the narrow section — it's **rounding the corner where the two sections meet** (a fillet). A sharp inside corner concentrates stress by a factor of 2-3x regardless of how thick either section is; a generous fillet there removes most of that concentration for free, no plate changes needed. That's the right move and costs nothing.

## 2. "Screw thread that goes into the plate" — this is the part I'd push back on

If you mean **printing actual helical threads directly onto the tenon** (so it screws into the plate like a bolt, no separate hardware) — I'd flag the same risk that killed the snap-fit idea a few days ago: printed threads at ~6mm diameter with M3-ish pitch are right at the edge of what a 0.4mm nozzle can resolve cleanly. They come out sloppy, strip easily in PETG, and — same as before — you get exactly one coupon print to find out if it worked, with no time to iterate a bad one. It's the identical failure mode your own spec already ruled out for Smart Blocks.

There's also a geometric wall here: the plate's pocket is a **blind pocket with a floor** — hex cavity for 2.5mm, then solid material with just a 3.2mm M3 hole underneath. There's no way for a wider threaded shaft to pass all the way through to the plate's outer face. So a "threaded tenon" only has a 2.5mm-deep hex cavity to bite into anyway, not a full through-thread.

## 3. "A cap that goes in like a nut" — I think this is already what we speced

This is genuinely the heat-set insert + thumbscrew plan from before: a **real brass thread** (not printed) lives inside the tenon, and a knurled thumbscrew — which *is* your "cap that acts like a nut" — clamps it from outside, hand-tight, no tools. The difference is just *where* the thread lives: in a proper brass insert instead of printed plastic, so it doesn't depend on unverified print tolerance.

So my honest read: **you already arrived at most of this** — you just described the insert+thumbscrew mechanism in different words while also reaching for printed threads, which is the one piece that reintroduces the exact risk we moved away from.

Want me to:
- Add the fillet at the tenon/shaft transition (quick, unambiguous win), and
- Keep the heat-set insert + thumbscrew as the actual "thread + cap"?

Or is there something specific pushing you toward eliminating the insert entirely (e.g. worried about sourcing them in Sétif)? If it's sourcing, that's worth knowing before I touch geometry — there's a fallback (plain M3 nut trapped in a printed hex pocket instead of a heat-set insert) that avoids needing that specific part at all.

import adsk.core, adsk.fusion, math, json, traceback

def run(context):
    try:
        app = adsk.core.Application.get()
        doc = app.activeDocument
        assert doc.name == 'Pillars', 'WRONG DOC: ' + doc.name
        root = app.activeProduct.rootComponent
        out = {}

        for f in list(root.features.threadFeatures):
            if f.name == 'NutThread': f.deleteMe()
        for f in list(root.features.extrudeFeatures):
            if f.name in ('NutBody','NutHole'): f.deleteMe()
        for s in list(root.sketches):
            if s.name in ('SK_NutHex','SK_NutHole'): s.deleteMe()

        AF = 0.57
        THK = 0.23
        HOLE_D = 0.2529
        OX, OY = 2.0, 0.0

        def hex_pts(af, ox, oy):
            R = (af/2.0) / math.cos(math.radians(30))
            return [adsk.core.Point3D.create(ox + R*math.cos(math.radians(30+60*k)),
                                             oy + R*math.sin(math.radians(30+60*k)), 0) for k in range(6)]

        sk = root.sketches.add(root.xYConstructionPlane)
        sk.name = 'SK_NutHex'
        pts = hex_pts(AF, OX, OY)
        lines = sk.sketchCurves.sketchLines
        first = lines.addByTwoPoints(pts[0], pts[1])
        prev = first.endSketchPoint
        for k in range(1,5):
            prev = lines.addByTwoPoints(prev, pts[k+1]).endSketchPoint
        lines.addByTwoPoints(prev, first.startSketchPoint)

        exts = root.features.extrudeFeatures
        ei = exts.createInput(sk.profiles.item(0), adsk.fusion.FeatureOperations.NewBodyFeatureOperation)
        ei.setDistanceExtent(False, adsk.core.ValueInput.createByReal(THK))
        f_nut = exts.add(ei); f_nut.name = 'NutBody'
        nut_body = root.bRepBodies.item(root.bRepBodies.count-1)
        nut_body.name = 'HexNut_M3_Body'

        sk2 = root.sketches.add(root.xYConstructionPlane)
        sk2.name = 'SK_NutHole'
        sk2.sketchCurves.sketchCircles.addByCenterRadius(adsk.core.Point3D.create(OX,OY,0), HOLE_D/2.0)
        ei2 = exts.createInput(sk2.profiles.item(0), adsk.fusion.FeatureOperations.CutFeatureOperation)
        ei2.participantBodies = [nut_body]
        ei2.setDistanceExtent(False, adsk.core.ValueInput.createByReal(THK))
        exts.add(ei2).name = 'NutHole'

        out['nut_volume_before_thread_cm3'] = round(nut_body.physicalProperties.volume,4)

        hole_face = None
        for fc in nut_body.faces:
            g = fc.geometry
            if g.surfaceType == adsk.core.SurfaceTypes.CylinderSurfaceType:
                hole_face = fc; break
        out['hole_face_found'] = hole_face is not None

        threads = root.features.threadFeatures
        faces_coll = adsk.core.ObjectCollection.create()
        faces_coll.add(hole_face)
        ti = adsk.fusion.ThreadInfo.create(False, True, 'ISO Metric profile', 'M3x0.5', '6H', True)
        tin = threads.createInput(faces_coll, ti)
        tin.isModeled = True
        tin.isFullLength = True
        tf = threads.add(tin)
        tf.name = 'NutThread'

        out['nut_volume_after_thread_cm3'] = round(nut_body.physicalProperties.volume,4)
        bb = nut_body.boundingBox

        AF = 0.57
        THK = 0.23
        HOLE_D = 0.2529
        OX, OY = 2.0, 0.0

        def hex_pts(af, ox, oy):
            R = (af/2.0) / math.cos(math.radians(30))
            return [adsk.core.Point3D.create(ox + R*math.cos(math.radians(30+60*k)),
                                             oy + R*math.sin(math.radians(30+60*k)), 0) for k in range(6)]

        for k in range(1,5):

        lines.addByTwoPoints(prev, first.startSketchPoint)

That matches your three reference pictures closely — threaded pillar end and a proper hex nut, side by side, real geometry, both in the same **Pillars** document.

## What's built

| Part | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Pillar** | 10mm AF hex shaft, real **M3×0.5 external thread** (class 6g) at both ends, 2.4mm long each |
| **Hex nut** | 5.7mm AF × 2.3mm thick, real **M3×0.5 internal thread** (class 6H), tapped through |

## How it fits your already-cut plate — no plate rework needed

Instead of the thread trying to reach through the plate's tiny 3.2mm floor hole, the **nut sits inside the hex pocket you already cut** (6.0mm AF × 2.5mm deep — almost exactly this nut's size) and the pillar's threaded stud screws straight into it. You drop the nut in the pocket, thread the pillar in from the opening, done — zero new cuts on the frozen plate.

| Check | Plate pocket | Nut | Fit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Across flats | 6.0mm (nominal) | 5.7mm | matches the same undersize allowance used for the old tenon |
| Depth | 2.5mm | 2.3mm thick | 0.2mm clearance |
| Stud reach | — | 2.4mm | fully engages nut, 0.1mm short of the pocket floor (won't bottom out) |

These are genuine ISO-standard cut threads, not a cosmetic decal — `isModeled: True` confirmed on all three thread features. def run(context):
    try:
        app = adsk.core.Application.get()
        doc = app.activeDocument
        assert doc.name == 'waffle plate'
        root = app.activeProduct.rootComponent
        body = [b for b in root.bRepBodies if b.name=='Body1'][0]
        log = {}

        for fname in ['M3_TabScrewHoles','HexSocket_Upper','HexSocket_Lower']:
            for f in list(root.features.extrudeFeatures):
                if f.name == fname: f.deleteMe()
        for sname in ['SK_M3_TabScrewHoles','SK_HexSocket_Upper','SK_HexSocket_Lower']:
            s = root.sketches.itemByName(sname)
            if s: s.deleteMe()
        for pname in ['PL_HexSocket_Upper','PL_HexSocket_Lower']:
            for p in list(root.constructionPlanes):
                if p.name == pname: p.deleteMe()

        log['volume_after_cleanup'] = round(body.physicalProperties.volume,4)

        AF = 10.0
        R = AF / math.sqrt(3.0)
        POCKET = 3.0

        a = 5.0 + 5.0*math.sqrt(3.0)
        b = 25.0 + 5.0*math.sqrt(3.0)
        E = 95.0

        LOWER, UPPER = [], []
        for sx in (1,-1):
            for sy in (1,-1):
                LOWER.append((sx*E, sy*a))
                LOWER.append((sx*b, sy*E))
                UPPER.append((sx*E, sy*b))
                UPPER.append((sx*a, sy*E))

        def make_hex(sk, cx, cy):
            lines = sk.sketchCurves.sketchLines
            sa = 0.0 if abs(abs(cx)-E) < 0.001 else 90.0
            pts = []
            for k in range(6):
                ang = math.radians(sa + 60.0*k)
                pts.append(adsk.core.Point3D.create((cx + R*math.cos(ang))/10.0,
                                                    (cy + R*math.sin(ang))/10.0, 0))
            first = lines.addByTwoPoints(pts[0], pts[1])
            prev = first.endSketchPoint
            for k in range(1,5):
                prev = lines.addByTwoPoints(prev, pts[k+1]).endSketchPoint
            lines.addByTwoPoints(prev, first.startSketchPoint)

        def cut_pockets(centers, top_z, label):
            pin = root.constructionPlanes.createInput()
            pin.setByOffset(root.xYConstructionPlane, adsk.core.ValueInput.createByReal(top_z/10.0))
            pl = root.constructionPlanes.add(pin); pl.name = 'PL_'+label
            sk = root.sketches.add(pl); sk.name = 'SK_'+label
            sk.isComputeDeferred = True
            for (cx, cy) in centers:
                make_hex(sk, cx, cy)
            sk.isComputeDeferred = False
            profs = adsk.core.ObjectCollection.create()
            for p in sk.profiles: profs.add(p)
            log[label+'_profiles'] = sk.profiles.count
            exts = root.features.extrudeFeatures
            ei = exts.createInput(profs, adsk.fusion.FeatureOperations.CutFeatureOperation)
            ei.participantBodies = [body]
            ei.setDistanceExtent(False, adsk.core.ValueInput.createByReal(-POCKET/10.0))
            f = exts.add(ei); f.name = label

        cut_pockets(LOWER, 5.0, 'HexSocket_Lower')
        cut_pockets(UPPER, 10.0, 'HexSocket_Upper')

        log['final_volume_cm3'] = round(body.physicalProperties.volume,4)
        log['final_face_count'] = body.faces.count
        print(json.dumps(log))
    except:
        print('ERROR: ' + traceback.format_exc())

That's a genuinely friendly-looking cap — smooth domed top, no exposed thread, distinct from the technical look of the pillar's visible external threads.

## Summary of both changes

| Change | What happened |
|---|---|
| **Plate pocket floor** | Cut a **Ø6.4mm through-hole** in all 16 tab floors, centered in each pocket — verified void through the full floor thickness, walls intact around it |
| **Nut → cap nut** | Blind M6×1.0 thread (2.2mm deep, stops short of the top), leaving a **solid 0.8mm closed cap**, then domed with a 3mm fillet on all 6 top edges for the rounded, friendly look in your reference |

**How it assembles now:** the pillar's threaded stud passes up through the plate's new floor hole from below, into the pocket, and threads into the cap nut sitting in the pocket — cap facing up, smooth and closed, hiding the thread entirely.

content.text:
Before I touch Fusion — the block system is a design conversation, not a modeling task. Let me be honest about what the plate actually gives us to work with, because the answer changes the whole approach.

## What the plate honestly offers for mounting

Recapping the measured facts, so we design against reality:

- **The hole field on the deck is decorative** — not a repeating grid. Pairs of same-diameter holes exist at all sorts of spacings (7, 3, 4, 2, 5, 1, 6mm…). Your spec's original "universal 2-hole footprint at 10mm pitch" was designed for a grid-based plate that was never built. Trying to force it onto this plate would give you maybe 3-4 usable mounting sites in weird places.
- **The 16 perimeter hex tabs are the reliable mounting real estate.** Each already has an M6 through-hole and a captive nut pocket — installed for pillars, but structurally they're also perfect block-mounting anchors. Positions are predictable, symmetric, and edge-facing (which matters — see below).
- **Four square cutouts in the middle deck** — those look intentional (probably for motor mounts, battery, driver board pass-throughs). Blocks shouldn't fight them.

## The important insight: blocks split naturally into two categories

They have genuinely different mounting needs, so trying to unify them with one "universal footprint" is a false economy:

**A. Outward-facing sensor blocks** (HC-SR04, IR distance, future LiDAR, status LEDs)
- Physically need to point outward from the chassis, unobstructed
- Need directional keying (HC-SR04 bolted backwards measures the chassis)
- Perimeter positions are natural for them
- **My proposal**: mount them on the hex tabs. Each block sits on top of a tab (or sandwiched between the two plates via the pillar), thread stays engaged, orientation is enforced by the tab's fixed radial direction

**B. Internal component holders** (ESP32 cradle, motor driver bracket, battery holder, wire management)
- Don't need to point outward, don't need to be swappable during a demo
- Placement is dictated by the component's own dimensions, not by a modular grid
- **My proposal**: purpose-built, not modular. Each one sized to its specific job, screwed to the deck through whichever holes happen to align

The spec's original vision was one universal system for both. Given the plate you actually have, splitting them costs nothing and delivers both jobs better.

## Two decisions before I model anything

content.text: Before I model anything, let me switch to your new file and then flag two real constraints on your chosen approaches — one is a geometric fitment problem I can't solve without your input, the other needs me to actually survey the deck holes before designing.

Good — new blank file is active, and the plate/pillar files are closed (which is fine, I have their measurements from earlier). Two things need decisions before I cut geometry.

## Problem 1: The tab top rim is too narrow for M3

I calculated the actual geometry. The tab is a hexagon 20mm across corners with a hex pocket 10mm across corners cut into its top face. That leaves a rim of material around the pocket that's:

- **3.66 mm wide** at the flats (narrowest direction)
- **4.23 mm wide** at the corners (widest direction)

An M3 clearance hole is Ø3.2mm. To place one in that rim, best case (at a corner), you'd have **0.5 mm of wall material on each side** of the hole. In PETG at 0.4mm nozzle, that's essentially a designed crack — the tab tip will split off the first time you tighten a screw.

Three ways out:

- **A. Downsize to M2 or M2.5** at the tab corners — walls become 0.9-1.2mm, marginal but printable
- **B. Make the block *become* the cap-nut** — the block's underside integrates the threaded cavity, so installing a block replaces a plain cap nut. Uses upper tabs (which don't hold pillars, per your earlier decision). No new plate holes, no fitment issue. Trade-off: blocks are locked to tab positions, one block per used tab.
- **C. Enlarge the tabs** — plate rework you've been trying to avoid

## Problem 2: I need to actually survey the deck holes

For the deck-mount block, I proposed "bolt through unused deck holes" without knowing which existing holes are actually usable. The plate's hole field is irregular — I need to find pairs at consistent spacing, in a region clear of both the central square cutouts and the perimeter tabs, before I know if the concept even works.

This is a ~5-minute analysis I need to do in the plate file — enumerate all hole coordinates, cluster by diameter, and find pairs at spacings that could accept a standard component (ESP32 DevKit V1 is my target — needs a ~48mm span between mount points).

## What I'm asking you

import adsk.core, json, math
from collections import defaultdict, Counter

def run(context):
    app = adsk.core.Application.get()
    root = app.activeProduct.rootComponent
    body = [b for b in root.bRepBodies if b.name=='Body1'][0]

    def mm(v): return round(v*10.0, 2)

    # collect unique hole centers grouped by diameter (from cylindrical faces)
    centers = defaultdict(set)
    for face in body.faces:
        g = face.geometry
        if g.surfaceType != adsk.core.SurfaceTypes.CylinderSurfaceType:
            continue
        cyl = adsk.core.Cylinder.cast(g)
        # only interested in vertical (Z-axis) cylinders — real holes, not hex pocket walls
        ax = cyl.axis
        if abs(abs(ax.z) - 1.0) > 0.01:
            continue
        d = round(cyl.radius*20, 2)
        centers[d].add((mm(cyl.origin.x), mm(cyl.origin.y)))

    # summarize
    summary = {}
    for d, pts in centers.items():
        summary[str(d)+'mm'] = len(pts)

    # focus on the deck-mount candidates: 4.5mm (most numerous)
    d45 = sorted(centers.get(4.5, []))

    # deck region only: exclude perimeter (r > 78mm) so we skip everything near the tabs
    deck = [(x,y) for (x,y) in d45 if math.hypot(x,y) <= 78]

    # compute pairwise distances (bounded, <60mm) for the deck subset
    distances = Counter()
    N = len(deck)
    for i in range(N):
        x1,y1 = deck[i]
        for j in range(i+1, N):
            x2,y2 = deck[j]
            dx = x2-x1; dy = y2-y1
            d = math.hypot(dx,dy)
            if d < 0.1 or d > 60: continue
            # bucket to 0.1mm resolution
            distances[round(d,1)] += 1

    top_dists = distances.most_common(20)

    print(json.dumps({
        'hole_counts_all': summary,
        'deck_4.5mm_count': len(deck),
        'top_pairwise_distances_mm': top_dists
    }))

        centers.add((mm(cyl.origin.x), mm(cyl.origin.y)))

    rectangles = []

The plate is more useful than I thought — there are **repeating rectangular hole patterns** clustered in symmetric positions. Here's what I found:

## 6 "module bays" on the deck

| Footprint | # of slots | Positions |
|---|---|---|
| **35 × 27 mm** | 4 slots | 4 corners: (±39.5, ±6.5) |
| **44 × 27 mm** | 2 slots | Centered on X=0: (0, ±6.5) |

All six are ~27mm tall, giving you a **symmetric 3×2 layout of module bays** across the deck. Every corner of every bay is a Ø4.5mm hole (M4 clearance) already in the plate.

Plus these repeating footprints elsewhere on the deck:

| Footprint | Count | Best-suited for |
|---|---|---|
| 21 × 40 mm | 8 instances | 2×18650 battery holder |
| 35 × 14 mm | 8 instances | small breakout modules |
| 12 × 14 mm | 8 instances | tiny modules (DRV8833, etc.) |
| 18 × 7.8 mm | 10 instances | very small (LED strip, tiny sensor) |

**Good news:** you actually have a modular system hidden in the plate. The 6 module bays are symmetric and repeating. A **universal deck bracket** designed to fit into any 44×27mm or 35×27mm slot would be plug-and-play across the deck.

- Total block height: ~20mm (well under the 40mm interplate spacing)
- Sensor faces radially outward — enforced by hex plug's 6-fold indexing on the hex tab (60° increments), so it can only point in 6 discrete directions. Radially-outward is one of them.

import adsk.core, adsk.fusion, math, json, traceback

def run(context):
    try:
        app = adsk.core.Application.get()
        doc = app.activeDocument
        assert doc.name == 'Untitled', 'WRONG DOC: ' + doc.name
        root = app.activeProduct.rootComponent
        log = {'active': doc.name}

        PLUG_AF = 0.97   # cm = 9.7mm across flats
        PLUG_H  = 0.27   # 2.7mm tall
        THREAD_MINOR_D = 0.5035
        THREAD_DEPTH = 0.20

        BASE_XMIN, BASE_XMAX = -0.6, 5.0
        BASE_YMIN, BASE_YMAX = -1.2, 1.2
        BASE_TOP = 0.57  # top of base at Z=5.7mm

        WALL_XMIN, WALL_XMAX = 0.5, 5.0
        WALL_INNER = 1.025
        WALL_OUTER = 1.225
        WALL_TOP = 2.07  # top of wall at Z=20.7mm

        exts = root.features.extrudeFeatures

        # ---- Layer 1: Hex plug (new body) ----
        def hex_pts(af, ox, oy):
            R = (af/2.0) / math.cos(math.radians(30))
            return [adsk.core.Point3D.create(ox + R*math.cos(math.radians(30+60*k)),
                                             oy + R*math.sin(math.radians(30+60*k)), 0) for k in range(6)]
        sk1 = root.sketches.add(root.xYConstructionPlane); sk1.name = 'SK_Plug'
        pts = hex_pts(PLUG_AF, 0, 0)
        lines = sk1.sketchCurves.sketchLines
        first = lines.addByTwoPoints(pts[0], pts[1])
        prev = first.endSketchPoint
        for k in range(1,5):
            prev = lines.addByTwoPoints(prev, pts[k+1]).endSketchPoint
        lines.addByTwoPoints(prev, first.startSketchPoint)
        ei = exts.createInput(sk1.profiles.item(0), adsk.fusion.FeatureOperations.NewBodyFeatureOperation)
        ei.setDistanceExtent(False, adsk.core.ValueInput.createByReal(PLUG_H))
        exts.add(ei).name = 'BlockPlug'
        block = root.bRepBodies.item(root.bRepBodies.count - 1)
        block.name = 'SensorBlock_HCSR04'
        log['plug_vol'] = round(block.physicalProperties.volume, 4)

        # ---- Layer 2: Blind M6 hole from bottom (Z=0 going UP into plug) ----
        sk2 = root.sketches.add(root.xYConstructionPlane); sk2.name = 'SK_BlindHole'
        sk2.sketchCurves.sketchCircles.addByCenterRadius(adsk.core.Point3D.create(0,0,0), THREAD_MINOR_D/2.0)
        ei2 = exts.createInput(sk2.profiles.item(0), adsk.fusion.FeatureOperations.CutFeatureOperation)
        ei2.participantBodies = [block]
        ei2.setDistanceExtent(False, adsk.core.ValueInput.createByReal(THREAD_DEPTH))
        exts.add(ei2).name = 'BlindThreadHole'

        # ---- Layer 3: Base platform (join) ----
        sk3 = root.sketches.add(root.xYConstructionPlane); sk3.name = 'SK_Base'
        p0 = adsk.core.Point3D.create(BASE_XMIN, BASE_YMIN, 0)
        p1 = adsk.core.Point3D.create(BASE_XMAX, BASE_YMAX, 0)
        sk3.sketchCurves.sketchLines.addTwoPointRectangle(p0, p1)
        # find the profile (there may be 2 if the hex plug's projection interferes; take the outer one)
        prof = None
        for pr in sk3.profiles:
            if pr.areaProperties().area > 10.0:  # in cm^2, base is 5.6*2.4=13.44 cm^2, plug ~0.008 cm^2
                prof = pr; break
        if prof is None:
            prof = max(sk3.profiles, key=lambda p: p.areaProperties().area)
        log['base_profile_area_cm2'] = round(prof.areaProperties().area, 4)
        # extrude from Z=PLUG_H upward
        pin = root.constructionPlanes.createInput()
        pin.setByOffset(root.xYConstructionPlane, adsk.core.ValueInput.createByReal(PLUG_H))
        pl_base = root.constructionPlanes.add(pin); pl_base.name = 'PL_Base'
        sk3b = root.sketches.add(pl_base); sk3b.name = 'SK_BaseUp'
        sk3b.sketchCurves.sketchLines.addTwoPointRectangle(
            adsk.core.Point3D.create(BASE_XMIN, BASE_YMIN, 0),
            adsk.core.Point3D.create(BASE_XMAX, BASE_YMAX, 0))
        prof2 = sk3b.profiles.item(0)
        ei3 = exts.createInput(prof2, adsk.fusion.FeatureOperations.JoinFeatureOperation)
        ei3.participantBodies = [block]
        ei3.setDistanceExtent(False, adsk.core.ValueInput.createByReal(BASE_TOP - PLUG_H))
        exts.add(ei3).name = 'BaseSlab'
        # remove SK_Base (unused)
        sk3.deleteMe()

        # ---- Layer 4: Left & Right walls ----
        pin_w = root.constructionPlanes.createInput()
        pin_w.setByOffset(root.xYConstructionPlane, adsk.core.ValueInput.createByReal(BASE_TOP))
        pl_wall = root.constructionPlanes.add(pin_w); pl_wall.name = 'PL_Walls'
        sk_w = root.sketches.add(pl_wall); sk_w.name = 'SK_Walls'
        # left wall (Y-negative)
        sk_w.sketchCurves.sketchLines.addTwoPointRectangle(
            adsk.core.Point3D.create(WALL_XMIN, -WALL_OUTER, 0),
            adsk.core.Point3D.create(WALL_XMAX, -WALL_INNER, 0))
        # right wall
        sk_w.sketchCurves.sketchLines.addTwoPointRectangle(
            adsk.core.Point3D.create(WALL_XMIN, WALL_INNER, 0),
            adsk.core.Point3D.create(WALL_XMAX, WALL_OUTER, 0))
        profs = adsk.core.ObjectCollection.create()
        for pr in sk_w.profiles: profs.add(pr)
        log['wall_profiles_count'] = sk_w.profiles.count
        ei4 = exts.createInput(profs, adsk.fusion.FeatureOperations.JoinFeatureOperation)
        ei4.participantBodies = [block]
        ei4.setDistanceExtent(False, adsk.core.ValueInput.createByReal(WALL_TOP - BASE_TOP))
        exts.add(ei4).name = 'Walls'

        log['final_vol_cm3'] = round(block.physicalProperties.volume, 4)
        bb = block.boundingBox
        log['bbox_mm'] = [round((bb.maxPoint.x-bb.minPoint.x)*10,2),
                          round((bb.maxPoint.y-bb.minPoint.y)*10,2),
                          round((bb.maxPoint.z-bb.minPoint.z)*10,2)]
        print(json.dumps(log))
    except:
        print('ERROR: ' + traceback.format_exc())

def run(context):

        app = adsk.core.Application.get()
        assert app.activeDocument.name == 'Untitled'
        root = app.activeProduct.rootComponent
        block = [b for b in root.bRepBodies if b.name=='SensorBlock_HCSR04'][0]
        out = {}

        # find the blind hole's cylindrical face (small radius, near origin)
        hole_face = None
        for fc in block.faces:
            g = fc.geometry
            if g.surfaceType != adsk.core.SurfaceTypes.CylinderSurfaceType:
                continue
            cyl = adsk.core.Cylinder.cast(g)
            r = round(cyl.radius*10, 3)
            if abs(r - 2.5175) < 0.05:
                hole_face = fc; break
        out['hole_face_found'] = hole_face is not None

        threads = root.features.threadFeatures
        coll = adsk.core.ObjectCollection.create()
        coll.add(hole_face)
        ti = adsk.fusion.ThreadInfo.create(False, True, 'ISO Metric profile', 'M6x1', '6H', True)
        tin = threads.createInput(coll, ti)

        front_face = None

            pln = adsk.core.Plane.cast(g)
            n = pln.normal
            if abs(n.x - 1.0) > 0.01: continue
            bb = fc.boundingBox
            # want the largest +X face near X=3.3cm at cradle height
            if abs(bb.minPoint.x - 0.33) > 0.01: continue
            if bb.maxPoint.z*10 < 25: continue  # skip small faces at low Z
            front_face = fc
            break
        out['front_face_found'] = front_face is not None
        if front_face:
            bb = front_face.boundingBox
            out['front_face_extents_mm'] = [round(bb.minPoint.y*10,2), round(bb.maxPoint.y*10,2),

            out['front_face_area_mm2'] = round(front_face.area*100,2)

        # sketch directly on the face - Fusion auto-defines UV from face geometry
        sk = root.sketches.add(front_face)
        sk.name = 'SK_CanHoles'

        # convert desired global (Y, Z) points to sketch's local coords via modelToSketchSpace
        pts_global = [(1.3, 2.07), (-1.3, 2.07)]  # (Y, Z) in cm

            local_pt = sk.modelToSketchSpace(world_pt)
            sk.sketchCurves.sketchCircles.addByCenterRadius(local_pt, 0.85)

        # extrude cut in the -X direction (into the body)
        profs = adsk.core.ObjectCollection.create()
        for pr in sk.profiles:

        out['can_profile_count'] = sk.profiles.count

        ei.setDistanceExtent(False, adsk.core.ValueInput.createByReal(-0.20))

Block is done as a v1. But before you take this as final, I need to flag **three issues** I noticed while building — one is genuinely wrong and worth fixing before you go further:

## Issue 1 (WRONG — affects function): plug orientation is 30° off

I built the hex plug with "point along +Y" (block's Y-axis), but the tab pockets in the plate have "point along the radial direction" from plate center. To make it fit, the block would need to rotate 30° when placed on a tab — which means **the transducers would face 30° off-radial**, detecting obstacles slightly to the side rather than straight ahead.

Fix: rebuild the plug hex with a different start angle. ~1 minute of work.

## Issue 2 (structural concern): cradle cantilevers off the shoulder

The cradle is 49.5mm long (Y-axis), but the hex shoulder underneath is only ~17mm. That leaves ~16mm of unsupported cradle sticking out each side. Under HC-SR04 weight + wire tension, PETG might flex or crack over time.

Fix options: extend the shoulder into a rectangle (aesthetically busier), or add triangular gussets between cradle and shoulder.

## Issue 3 (missing features for real use):

- **No PCB retention** — the sensor slides in but nothing holds it. Small clip or friction pad needed.
- **No cable slot** — HC-SR04 pins stick from one end of the PCB; wires need to exit somewhere. Currently they'd have to bend awkwardly around the cradle.

## Current dimensions (measured)

| Feature | Value |
|---|---|
| Overall bbox | 15 × 49.5 × 30.7 mm |
| Plug | 9.7mm AF hex × 2.7mm |
| Blind thread | M6×1.0 (real thread) × 2mm deep |
| Shoulder | 15mm AF hex × 3mm |
| Cradle exterior | 6.6 × 49.5 × 25mm |
| PCB slot | 2.6 × 45.5 × 22mm |
| Can openings | Ø17mm at Y=±13mm, Z=20.7mm |
| Volume | 5.414 cm³ |

import adsk.core, adsk.fusion, math, json, traceback

def run(context):
    try:
        app = adsk.core.Application.get()
        assert app.activeDocument.name == 'Untitled'
        root = app.activeProduct.rootComponent
        log = {}

        # ---- Clean slate: remove all existing features and bodies ----
        for f in list(root.features.threadFeatures):
            f.deleteMe()
        for f in list(root.features.extrudeFeatures):
            f.deleteMe()
        for s in list(root.sketches):
            s.deleteMe()
        for p in list(root.constructionPlanes):
            p.deleteMe()
        for b in list(root.bRepBodies):
            b.deleteMe()
        log['after_cleanup_bodies'] = root.bRepBodies.count

        # ---- Parameters ----
        PLUG_AF = 0.97          # cm, hex plug across flats
        PLUG_H = 0.27           # 2.7mm tall
        SHOULDER_AF = 1.5       # 15mm across flats
        SHOULDER_H = 0.3        # 3mm
        PLATFORM_X = 3.0        # 30mm long (radial direction when mounted)
        PLATFORM_Y = 2.2        # 22mm wide (tangential)
        PLATFORM_H = 0.3        # 3mm thick
        THREAD_MINOR_D = 0.5035
        THREAD_DEPTH = 0.20

        # ---- Hex plug (sa=0 -> points along X = radial direction) ----
        def hex_pts(af, ox, oy, sa_deg):
            R = (af/2.0) / math.cos(math.radians(30))
            return [adsk.core.Point3D.create(ox + R*math.cos(math.radians(sa_deg+60*k)),
                                             oy + R*math.sin(math.radians(sa_deg+60*k)), 0) for k in range(6)]

        def add_hex(sk, af, ox, oy, sa_deg):
            pts = hex_pts(af, ox, oy, sa_deg)
            lines = sk.sketchCurves.sketchLines
            first = lines.addByTwoPoints(pts[0], pts[1])
            prev = first.endSketchPoint
            for k in range(1,5):
                prev = lines.addByTwoPoints(prev, pts[k+1]).endSketchPoint
            lines.addByTwoPoints(prev, first.startSketchPoint)

        exts = root.features.extrudeFeatures

        # Layer 1: Plug
        sk1 = root.sketches.add(root.xYConstructionPlane); sk1.name = 'SK_Plug'
        add_hex(sk1, PLUG_AF, 0, 0, 0)  # sa=0 -> POINTS ALONG X (radial)
        ei = exts.createInput(sk1.profiles.item(0), adsk.fusion.FeatureOperations.NewBodyFeatureOperation)
        ei.setDistanceExtent(False, adsk.core.ValueInput.createByReal(PLUG_H))
        exts.add(ei).name = 'Plug'
        block = root.bRepBodies.item(0)
        block.name = 'UniversalSensorBlock'

        # Layer 2: Blind thread hole (M6 bore from bottom face)
        sk2 = root.sketches.add(root.xYConstructionPlane); sk2.name = 'SK_ThreadHole'
        sk2.sketchCurves.sketchCircles.addByCenterRadius(adsk.core.Point3D.create(0,0,0), THREAD_MINOR_D/2.0)
        ei2 = exts.createInput(sk2.profiles.item(0), adsk.fusion.FeatureOperations.CutFeatureOperation)
        ei2.participantBodies = [block]
        ei2.setDistanceExtent(False, adsk.core.ValueInput.createByReal(THREAD_DEPTH))
        exts.add(ei2).name = 'ThreadHole'

        # Apply M6x1.0 internal thread
        hole_face = None
        for fc in block.faces:
            g = fc.geometry
            if g.surfaceType == adsk.core.SurfaceTypes.CylinderSurfaceType:
                cyl = adsk.core.Cylinder.cast(g)
                r = round(cyl.radius*10, 3)
                if abs(r - 2.5175) < 0.05:
                    hole_face = fc; break
        threads = root.features.threadFeatures
        coll = adsk.core.ObjectCollection.create(); coll.add(hole_face)
        ti = adsk.fusion.ThreadInfo.create(False, True, 'ISO Metric profile', 'M6x1', '6H', True)
        tin = threads.createInput(coll, ti)
        tin.isModeled = True; tin.isFullLength = True
        threads.add(tin).name = 'InternalThread'

        # Layer 3: Shoulder hex
        pin_sh = root.constructionPlanes.createInput()
        pin_sh.setByOffset(root.xYConstructionPlane, adsk.core.ValueInput.createByReal(PLUG_H))
        pl_sh = root.constructionPlanes.add(pin_sh); pl_sh.name = 'PL_Shoulder'
        sk3 = root.sketches.add(pl_sh); sk3.name = 'SK_Shoulder'
        add_hex(sk3, SHOULDER_AF, 0, 0, 0)  # sa=0
        ei3 = exts.createInput(sk3.profiles.item(0), adsk.fusion.FeatureOperations.JoinFeatureOperation)
        ei3.participantBodies = [block]
        ei3.setDistanceExtent(False, adsk.core.ValueInput.createByReal(SHOULDER_H))
        exts.add(ei3).name = 'Shoulder'

        # Layer 4: Platform
        pin_pf = root.constructionPlanes.createInput()
        pin_pf.setByOffset(root.xYConstructionPlane, adsk.core.ValueInput.createByReal(PLUG_H + SHOULDER_H))
        pl_pf = root.constructionPlanes.add(pin_pf); pl_pf.name = 'PL_Platform'
        sk4 = root.sketches.add(pl_pf); sk4.name = 'SK_Platform'
        sk4.sketchCurves.sketchLines.addTwoPointRectangle(
            adsk.core.Point3D.create(-PLATFORM_X/2, -PLATFORM_Y/2, 0),
            adsk.core.Point3D.create(PLATFORM_X/2, PLATFORM_Y/2, 0))
        prof_pf = sk4.profiles.item(0)
        ei4 = exts.createInput(prof_pf, adsk.fusion.FeatureOperations.JoinFeatureOperation)
        ei4.participantBodies = [block]
        ei4.setDistanceExtent(False, adsk.core.ValueInput.createByReal(PLATFORM_H))
        exts.add(ei4).name = 'Platform'

        # Layer 5: Zip-tie slots (4 of them, at platform corners)
        # Each slot: 2mm wide (X) x 6mm long (Y), inset 3mm from platform corners
        pin_sl = root.constructionPlanes.createInput()
        pin_sl.setByOffset(root.xYConstructionPlane, adsk.core.ValueInput.createByReal(PLUG_H + SHOULDER_H + PLATFORM_H))
        pl_sl = root.constructionPlanes.add(pin_sl); pl_sl.name = 'PL_Slots'
        sk5 = root.sketches.add(pl_sl); sk5.name = 'SK_ZipTieSlots'
        SLOT_W = 0.20  # 2mm
        SLOT_L = 0.60  # 6mm
        # Corner positions: inset 3mm from platform edge, centered
        inset_x = PLATFORM_X/2 - 0.6  # 3mm from edge, then slot half-width
        inset_y = PLATFORM_Y/2 - 0.45  # ~4.5mm from edge for slot half-length
        # Slot orientation: long axis along Y (2mm X width, 6mm Y length)
        for sx in (-1, 1):
            for sy in (-1, 1):
                cx = sx * inset_x
                cy = sy * inset_y
                sk5.sketchCurves.sketchLines.addTwoPointRectangle(
                    adsk.core.Point3D.create(cx - SLOT_W/2, cy - SLOT_L/2, 0),
                    adsk.core.Point3D.create(cx + SLOT_W/2, cy + SLOT_L/2, 0))
        slot_profs = adsk.core.ObjectCollection.create()
        for pr in sk5.profiles: slot_profs.add(pr)
        log['slot_profiles'] = sk5.profiles.count
        ei5 = exts.createInput(slot_profs, adsk.fusion.FeatureOperations.CutFeatureOperation)
        ei5.participantBodies = [block]
        ei5.setDistanceExtent(False, adsk.core.ValueInput.createByReal(-PLATFORM_H))
        exts.add(ei5).name = 'ZipTieSlots'

        # Layer 6: Cable exit slot in center of platform
        sk6 = root.sketches.add(pl_sl); sk6.name = 'SK_CableSlot'
        CABLE_W = 0.30  # 3mm
        CABLE_L = 1.0   # 10mm
        sk6.sketchCurves.sketchLines.addTwoPointRectangle(
            adsk.core.Point3D.create(-CABLE_L/2, -CABLE_W/2, 0),
            adsk.core.Point3D.create(CABLE_L/2, CABLE_W/2, 0))
        ei6 = exts.createInput(sk6.profiles.item(0), adsk.fusion.FeatureOperations.CutFeatureOperation)
        ei6.participantBodies = [block]
        ei6.setDistanceExtent(False, adsk.core.ValueInput.createByReal(-PLATFORM_H))
        exts.add(ei6).name = 'CableSlot'

        log['final_vol_cm3'] = round(block.physicalProperties.volume, 4)
        bb = block.boundingBox
        log['bbox_mm'] = [round((bb.maxPoint.x-bb.minPoint.x)*10,2),
                          round((bb.maxPoint.y-bb.minPoint.y)*10,2),
                          round((bb.maxPoint.z-bb.minPoint.z)*10,2)]
        app.activeViewport.fit()
        print(json.dumps(log))
    except:
        print('ERROR: ' + traceback.format_exc())

Done. Here's what you have.

## Universal Sensor Block v1

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Overall size | 30 × 22 × 8.7 mm |
| Volume | 2.503 cm³ (less than half the HC-SR04 version) |
| Mount | Hex plug 9.7mm AF + M6×1.0 blind thread (same as cap nut — no new hardware) |
| Plug orientation | POINT along +X = correctly aligns to tab pocket, no 30° tilt |
| Platform | 30 × 22 × 3 mm flat |
| Zip-tie slots | 4 × (2 × 6mm) at platform corners |
| Cable exit slot | 10 × 3mm at platform center |

## How it works

You place any small sensor PCB flat on top of the platform, then run one or two zip ties through the corner slots (crossing over the PCB) to strap it down. Cable exits through the central slot. Works for:

- **IMU boards** (MPU6050, BNO085) — flat mount, cables straight down
- **Any breakout with mounting holes** — either use the holes OR just zip-tie
- **PCBs without mounting holes** — zip-tie only, works fine
- **HC-SR04** — mounts flat, but the transducers would face UP instead of radially outward (see caveat below)

## Honest caveat about HC-SR04

Because the platform is horizontal and the block orientation on the tab is fixed (only 60° rotation options), an HC-SR04 sitting flat here would face UP or DOWN, not radially outward. For obstacle avoidance you want it facing forward.

Two paths from here:
- **Design a small vertical adapter** (an L-bracket that clips onto this platform, holds the HC-SR04 vertical facing outward). Keeps the base universal, adds a sensor-specific piece.
- **Add a small vertical wall** on the outboard end of the platform (blocks radial-facing-up but works for radial-facing-forward sensors). Less universal but one-piece.

Both are 5-10 min of work when you want them. Which — or leave it and let the platform be truly generic and add adapters only when specific sensors need them?

content.text: I can see the U-shape with pincher walls. Let me look from an angle that shows the lip clearly — an end view to see the C-channel cross-section.

Clear now — that's a proper pincher clip. From this end view you can see:
- Two vertical walls forming a slot
- Small inward-pointing lips at the top of each wall (the "hook" that traps the PCB)
- Platform below with hex shoulder and plug hanging down

## How the pincher works

- **PCB slot width:** 23mm (between walls at base)
- **Under-lip opening:** 21mm (lips project 1mm inward each side)
- **Insertion:** push PCB down between walls — walls flex outward, PCB snaps under lips
- **Removal:** flex one wall outward with a finger, lift PCB

## Final specs

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Overall size | 32 × 26 × 12.7 mm |
| Volume | 3.611 cm³ |
| PCB slot | 23mm wide × 32mm long (in Y × X) |
| PCB thickness clearance | up to ~3mm (from platform to lip underside) |
| Walls | 1.5mm thick, 4mm tall |
| Lips | 1mm inward × 1mm tall |
| Cable slot | 10 × 3mm at platform center |
| Mount | Hex plug 9.7mm AF + M6×1.0 blind thread (unchanged) |

## Fits

- **PCBs 21-23mm wide × up to 32mm long:** snap fit under lips (secure)
- **PCBs 15-20mm wide:** slot with a bit of play (still held by lips, might rattle)
- **PCBs >23mm wide (like HC-SR04 at 20mm × 45mm):** width fine, but LENGTH will overhang platform on both ends — cans on one end, pins on other. Actually HC-SR04 fits perfectly on Y (20mm PCB in 23mm slot) but its 45mm length exceeds the 32mm platform — 6.5mm overhang on each end. Not held there, but the middle 32mm is clipped down. HC-SR04 should still work — it's stiff enough that end support isn't critical.
- **Round or oddly-shaped PCBs:** won't work with pinchers — need a different mount.

## What I'm calling out as **NEEDS TESTING**

- **Snap force** — the 1mm lip depth and 1.5mm PETG wall flex is a first guess. If the PCB is too hard to insert or pops out too easily, the lip depth or wall thickness needs adjusting on the coupon.
- **Wall flex durability** — repeated PCB swaps flex the PETG walls. Might fatigue over many cycles. For a demo (a few swaps) it's fine.

Want to iterate on the pincher dimensions (wall thickness, lip depth, slot width), keep going with adapters for HC-SR04, or move on to something else?

content.text:
A mini vise — one fixed jaw, one sliding jaw, a bolt pulls them together. That's the right call for "universal": it adapts to any PCB width instead of being built for one.

**How it'll work:**
- **Fixed jaw** on one end, part of the base
- **Sliding jaw** is a separate printed piece that rides in a guide groove so it can't twist
- **M3 bolt** goes through the fixed jaw, runs under the PCB, and threads into an M3 nut trapped in the sliding jaw. Tightening pulls the jaws together and clamps the PCB edges in grooves on both jaw faces
- It uses a standard M3 bolt and nut, which are already on your shopping list, rather than a printed thread

The mini vise is built and verified. It's in the Untitled file, which isn't saved yet. The fixed jaw is on the left, with the recessed bolt hole on its outer face. The sliding jaw is on the right and rides in the guide groove. Both jaws have a PCB groove on their facing sides.

**How you use it:**
1. Drop an M3 nut into the hex slot on the back of the sliding jaw.
2. Push an M3 bolt through the fixed jaw from outside, under where the PCB will sit, and into the nut.
3. Put the PCB edges into the two jaw grooves and tighten the bolt. The sliding jaw pulls in and clamps the PCB.
4. To release, loosen the bolt and slide the jaw back by hand. It doesn't spring back on its own.

| Spec | Value |
|---|---|
| PCB width it holds | about 8 to 38mm |
| PCB thickness | up to 2mm (grooves are 2mm tall, 1.5mm deep) |
| Space under the PCB | about 4.8mm above the bolt, enough for pins poking through |
| Hardware | one M3 nut and one M3 bolt: M3×40 covers most PCB widths, M3×50 for the widest |
| Plate mount | same hex plug and M6 thread as the other parts, so no plate changes |
| Parts | two prints: the base with the fixed jaw, and the sliding jaw |

**Needs testing on your coupon print:**
- The sliding jaw's rail has 0.3mm of play on each side. If it wobbles, tighten that gap. If it jams, widen it.
- The nut slot is 5.8mm across flats for a 5.5mm nut. If the nut falls out, shrink it a little.

This holds the PCB **flat**. That's right for an IMU, but an HC-SR04 held flat would point its sensors straight up. If you want it pointing outward, I can angle the grooves so the jaws hold the board standing upright. It's the same vise, just a different groove direction.

content.text:
A rack and pinion can work, but it has one big catch compared to the screw.

**The catch: it doesn't hold on its own.** A screw is self-locking, so once you tighten it, the clamping force can't turn it back. A rack and pinion runs backwards easily. The PCB pushing back on the jaws would just spin the gear and open the clamp. So you'd need to add a lock: either a **ratchet** (a small pawl that clicks into the teeth and only lets it move one way) or a **friction lock** (a thumbscrew that pinches the gear's shaft).

**The upside: self-centering.** Put the gear in the middle and give each jaw its own rack on opposite sides of it. Turning one knob then moves **both jaws inward at the same time**, so the PCB always ends up centered, like a drill chuck. The screw version can't do that.

**Print limits:** the teeth need to be fairly coarse, around 1mm tooth size (module 1) or bigger. Smaller than that, PETG teeth come out mushy and strip.

My recommendation:
- **If you just want it to clamp reliably,** keep the screw. It's simpler, needs no lock, and has nothing that can strip.
- **If you want the self-centering (it also looks better for the jury),** go rack and pinion: one gear in the center with a knob on top, two racks each attached to a jaw, and a ratchet to hold it. A ratchet is nicer to use than a thumbscrew: you turn the knob until it's tight, then press the pawl to release.

Which do you want: screw, or rack and pinion with self-centering, and if so, ratchet or thumbscrew lock?

content.text:
That's basically the vise I already built: a screw along the bed moving one jaw toward a fixed jaw. But this one has two upgrades worth copying:

1. **The screw drives both ways.** In that vise the screw is held in place at the end (it spins but can't slide), so turning it **opens the jaw as well as closing it**. In mine, loosening the bolt only frees the jaw and you slide it back by hand. The fix is small: add a nut on the inside face of the fixed jaw, snug but not tight. Then the bolt can spin but can't move lengthwise, and the nut trapped in the sliding jaw carries the jaw both directions.

2. **A T-handle, so no tools.** You wanted tool-free assembly earlier, and this fits. I'd make a small printed knob (a T-bar or knurled wheel) that press-fits over the M3 bolt head, with a hex pocket so it can't slip. Turn it by hand and you're done.

One detail I'd skip: that vise's jaw rides in a slotted bed. My guide groove plus tongue already does the same job at this size.

Want me to add both? It's the nut recess on the fixed jaw plus a separate knob part.
